newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES CUSHION DECLINE, INCH 0.10PCT HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES CUSHION DECLINE, INCH 0.10PCT HIGHER.

text.p: Greek shares inched 0.10 percent higher on Wednesday, rebounding from early session lows on the back of Tuesday's mild price correction.
Industrials were upbeat, providing support to the broader market which was pulled down by banks due to ErgoBank shares going ex-dividend today.
ErgoBank paid a 950 drachma dividend per share for fiscal 1996. The effect on the bourse's general index was estimated at 0.38 percent.
Brokers said the market steadied itself with an intra-day correction which was fully absorbed by demand.

"Prices stabilised on Wednesday's session following an intra-day correction which was turned around by fresh buying interest at slightly lower price levels," said Evangelos Haratsis, broker at Beta Securities.
The market was seen consolidating at current levels in the near-term in the absence of adverse news.
"This year's rally has been steep and long-lasting, yet there appear to be no economic or political news on the horizon which may spook the market," Haratsis said.
Prices are seen consolidating for a while with renewed buying interest raising underlying support, he added.
Shares of Xiosbank were actively traded and hotly pursued on their second day of listing. Xiosbank shares nearly doubled to 6,328 drachmas with open buy interest for some 83,000 shares.
Brokers were pleased to see the level of demand for the issue which lured several new retail investors into the stock market.

"It is a good omen to see surprisingly high demand for a new listing such as Xiosbank. It stemmed mostly from retail investors, a large number of which made their debut to equity investing," Haratsis said.
This is indicative of the magnitude of underlying demand at going price levels, he added.
The Athens general index were weak at open, reaching a low of 1,694.28, but recovered to settled a net 0.10 percent or 1.77 points higher at 1,715.82.
Banks were off 0.60 percent impacted by ErgoBank but industrials advanced 1.38 percent with other sectors offering a mixed view at close.
Turnover eased from recent high levels, but still amounted to 25.6 billion drachmas in volume of 6.2 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 114 to 104 with 36 stocks unchanged on 254 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,108-1,138. Shares of OTE telecom , the underlying, were down 20 drachmas to 6,830.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted higher at 728.30-774.79. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $95.99-$97.68. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 4,215-4,450 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $23.52-$25.22. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted higher at 319-353 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
